name: A Las Cruces lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Las Cruces (Q33264), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A fenced suburban lot on the edge of the Mesilla Valley: gravel and bare soil instead of a lawn, watered only in a strip by the house, with mesquite, a yucca and agave round the edges and an apple for shade. Doves and grackles work the ground, quail walk the gravel, roadrunners patrol the fence line, and after dark a pallid bat leaves the porch eave to hunt scorpions over the dust.

facts.text: Las Cruces has a cool desert climate (Köppen BWk).

source.title: Wikipedia: Las Cruces, New Mexico

facts.text: Las Cruces is the economic and geographic centre of the Mesilla Valley, the agricultural region on the floodplain of the Rio Grande, and lies in Doña Ana County at about 1,191 metres above sea level.

source.title: Wikipedia: Las Cruces, New Mexico
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Las Cruces, New Mexico", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Chihuahuan Desert's dominant plant is the creosote bush, and yucca and numerous Opuntia cacti are abundant on slopes and uplands through most of it.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chihuahuan Desert

facts.text: The Chihuahuan Desert receives about 235 mm of rain a year, more than most other warm desert ecoregions, which is enough for mesquite and cottonwood to grow along the river.

source.title: Wikipedia: Chihuahuan Desert
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Chihuahuan Desert", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The greater roadrunner is New Mexico's state bird, and is abundant in the southeast of the state.

source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "New Mexico", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The white-winged dove is popular as a game bird, and has proved adaptable to human environments, expanding outside its historic range into northern New Mexico.

facts.text: Pallid bats eat Arizona bark scorpions, the most venomous scorpions in North America, and carry missense mutations in their voltage-gated sodium channels that appear to be responsible for that resistance.
